result.question: Examine the role of differentiated banks and other institutions in furthering financial inclusion in India. (Answer in 150 words)

directives.meaning: Look into the issue in detail: its causes, effects and implications.

sentences.text: Financial inclusion means affordable access to savings, credit, payments, insurance and pensions for underserved sections.
NABARD serves as the apex body coordinating the activities of all institutions involved in rural finance.
Commercial banks, regional rural banks and cooperatives together form a multi-agency structure for rural credit.
Self-help groups pool the small savings of members, mostly women, and lend to needy members without collateral.
Small finance banks were licensed to provide savings products and credit to small farmers, micro and small enterprises and other unorganised sector entities.
Payments banks can accept savings and current account deposits and offer payment and remittance services.
Payments banks can also extend small loans to migrant labourers and low-income households.
The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana opened basic accounts for unbanked households, which now serve as channels for direct benefit transfers.
The Unified Payments Interface, operated by the National Payments Corporation of India, has made low-value digital payments widespread.
Deeper inclusion now needs financial literacy, last-mile connectivity and productive credit that turns accounts into livelihoods.
